headline: North Korea fires ~10 short-range ballistic missiles from Wonsan into East Sea amid Korea border tensions
dek: [VERIFIED FACT for launch; ATTRIBUTED REPORT for type] North Korea fired around 10 (Straits Times: 'around a dozen') short-range ballistic missiles from the Wonsan area toward the East Sea at ~12:30 KST on Oct 29; they flew ~250 km. South Korea's JCS says surveillance was stepped up and…
sources: South Korea Joint Chiefs of Staff statement, carried by Reuters; Japan Defence Ministry via Yonhap; South Korea presidential National Security Office statement
fault_line: Show of force or prelude? Is this a routine border-pressure salvo ahead of the Oct 31 loudspeaker deadline, or the opening move in a wider Korean escalation that bypasses Seoul in any Trump-Kim track?

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT for launch; ATTRIBUTED REPORT for type] North Korea fired around 10 (Straits Times: 'around a dozen') short-range ballistic missiles from the Wonsan area toward the East Sea at ~12:30 KST on Oct 29; they flew ~250 km. South Korea's JCS says surveillance was stepped up and information shared closely with the US and Japan; Seoul's National Security Office convened an emergency meeting and called the launches a 'serious violation' of UN Security Council resolutions. Japan's Defence Ministry said the projectiles did not appear to land in Japan's EEZ. Context: first North Korean ballistic launch in 17 days (last Oct 12); tensions follow Sept 21 DMZ mine blasts wounding 3 South Korean soldiers, Seoul's proposal of border-clarification talks (unanswered), and Pyongyang's end-of-month deadline to reactivate propaganda loudspeakers. Korean press speculation that the salvo may have been KN-25 600mm multiple-rocket-launcher fire is UNCONFIRMED analysis, not a JCS finding.
sections.what_verified: 3+ declared families: Reuters T1 (launch, range, JCS statement, Japan position) + The Hindu T2 (barrage, Kim China visit, mine-blast context) + Yonhap T2 (Japan Defence Ministry position via AnewZ carry) + Straits Times T3 (around a dozen, AI torpedo/hypersonic context). Count varies by carrier ('around 10' vs 'around a dozen') -- report as 'around 10' per JCS via Reuters, noting the variance.
sections.what_disputed: No counter-claim on the launch itself. Pyongyang has not (in retrieved material) commented; Seoul's attribution of the Sept 21 mine blasts to North Korea is denied by Pyongyang. The KN-25 reading is Korean-press speculation only; JCS says exact specifications are under detailed analysis with the US.
sections.why_matters: 10 missiles, 250 km, one deadline: Pyongyang fires its first salvo in 17 days as its Oct 31 loudspeaker deadline arrives. Lead with the JCS number and the border-mine backstory, not the KN-25 speculation.

Lead with the JCS number and the border-mine backstory, not the KN-25 speculation. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Show of force or prelude?
